dervis-irab:38-52.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَقَوَّلَ) al-taqawwul: the ifti'āl form of speaking (qawl), because it involves an effort on the part of the one who does it. Abū Ḥayyān said: «al-taqawwul is for a person to say about another that he said something he did not say».
(الْأَقاوِيلِ) a plural of a plural, namely of أقوال, like بيت, أبيات and أبابيت. Al-Zamakhsharī said: He called the fabricated sayings أقاويل to diminish and belittle them, as when you say الأعاجيب and الأضاحيك, as though it were the plural of an uf'ūla from qawl.
(الْوَتِينَ) a vein in the heart from which blood flows to all the veins; its plural is وتن and أوتنة.

* I'rab:
(فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِما تُبْصِرُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive and lā is redundant (zāʾida); the discussion of lā before an oath has preceded at His words فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم. أقسم is an imperfect verb and its agent (fāʿil) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anā"; بما is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أقسم; تبصرون is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). In al-Bayḍāwī: «"So I do not swear" because the matter is evident and needs no confirmation by an oath; or "So I swear", with lā redundant; or "So no" is a rejection of their denial of the resurrection, and أقسم is resumptive». Al-Bayḍāwī's first view, i.e. making it negate the oath, is refuted by the specification of what is sworn by in His words بما تبصرون وما لا تبصرون. (وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ) conjoined to ما تبصرون. (إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ) inna and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and قول رسول is its khabar (predicate); كريم is an adjective of رسول. The clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of the oath, so it is what is sworn upon. The pronoun refers to the Qur'an, i.e. the Messenger said it, conveying it from Allah. (وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction and mā is the Ḥijāzī negative; هو is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and قول is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of the Ḥijāzī mā; شاعر is muḍāf ilayhi. قليلا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or an adjective of an omitted time, so it is an adverb of time, i.e. "you believe with little belief" or "for a little time". Mā may be negative, so that their belief is negated altogether; or it may be maṣdariyya, and what is qualified by littleness is linguistic belief, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the nominative as the agent of قليلا, i.e. "little is your belief"; or it may be redundant and emphatic. Perhaps this last view is the most correct of the views, because it is the one suited to emphasising the littleness. The meaning is that they believed in a few of the good things the Prophet ﷺ brought, such as maintaining kinship ties and chastity, and they only believed in these things because they ran in accordance with their natures and were in harmony with the requirements of their sense of honour. (وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ) conjoined to the previous clause and parallel to it in its i'rab. (تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a revelation"; من رب العالمين is attached to تنزيل. (وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ) The wāw is a conjunction and law is conditional; تقوّل is a past verb and its agent refers to the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Ḥayyān showed courtesy and said it refers to the implied fabricator and does not refer to the noble Messenger ﷺ, because of the impossibility of that occurring from him. Abū Ḥayyān said: «We reject that this be even by way of supposition in his case, upon him be blessing and peace». علينا is attached to تقوّل, and بعض الأقاويل is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq). (لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ) The lām occurs in the apodosis of law; أخذنا is a verb and its agent; منه is attached to أخذنا. In باليمين the bāʾ may be in its original sense, not redundant, the meaning being "We would have seized him with power from Us", so the bāʾ is circumstantial and the ḥāl (circumstantial) is from the agent, and منه is then in the status of a redundant element; or the bāʾ may be redundant, the meaning being "We would have seized his right hand". (ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ) ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; لقطعنا is conjoined to لأخذنا; منه is attached to قطعنا or to an omitted ḥāl; الوتين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction and mā is the Ḥijāzī negative; منكم is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of أحد and when it was put first it became a ḥāl; min is a redundant preposition and أحد is genitive in form and nominative in position as the noun of mā; عنه is attached to حاجزين, and حاجزين is the khabar of mā because it is the focus of the information. Al-Ḥawfī and al-Zamakhsharī said حاجزين is an adjective of أحد according to its form, and made plural according to its meaning, because it has the meaning of a group: in general negation it applies to singular and plural, masculine and feminine. On this i'rab أحد is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is منكم. Abū Ḥayyān judged this i'rab weak; he said: «This view is weak because the negation then falls on the khabar, which is its being from among you, and so does not fall on the preventing; whereas if حاجزين is the khabar, the negation falls on it, and the meaning becomes: there is no one among you who would prevent Him from what He wants to do to him of that. The pronoun in عنه refers to the killing, i.e. no one among you is able to prevent Him from that and ward it off from him; or to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, i.e. you are not able to keep the killer away from him and come between them. The address is to the people». The wording of al-Jalāl: «حاجزين, "preventers", is the khabar of mā; it is plural because أحد in a negative context has the meaning of a plural. The pronoun of عنه is for the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. there is no one preventing Us from him with respect to the punishment». The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «Min is redundant and أحد is a mubtadaʾ. There are two views on the khabar. The first is حاجزين; it is plural according to the meaning of أحد and would be genitive according to the form of أحد. [Translator's note: the source reads «وجر على لفظ أحد», which appears to be a transcription problem; the sense is presumably that it is plural by meaning while أحد is singular in form.] And it is said that it is accusative by mā, and منكم was not counted as a separation; منكم on this view is a ḥāl from أحد, and it is said it is for clarification. The second is that the khabar is منكم, and عن is attached to حاجزين». (وَإِنَّهُ لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction and the statement is conjoined to the preceding answer of the oath, so it is part of what is sworn by [Translator's note: the source says «المقسم به», "what is sworn by"; the sense is presumably "what is sworn upon" (المقسم عليه)], and what is between them is a parenthesis. Inna and its noun, the pronoun referring to the Qur'an; the shifted lām; تذكرة is the khabar, and للمتقين is attached to تذكرة. (وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ) also conjoined. Inna and its noun, the shifted lām, and the clause نعلم is the khabar; anna and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of نعلم; منكم is the fronted khabar of anna and مكذبين its delayed noun. (وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ) also conjoined; inna, its noun and its khabar; على الكافرين is an adjective of حسرة or attached to it. (وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ) also conjoined; inna, its noun and its khabar. (فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; سبّح is an imperative verb and باسم ربك is attached to سبّح, or the bāʾ is redundant; the i'rab of its like has preceded. العظيم is an adjective of ربك.

dervis-irab:1-8.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْحَاقَّةُ) the Resurrection and the Hour, whose occurrence is necessary. It is an active participle from حقّ الشيء, meaning: the thing became necessary. More will be said about it in the section on rhetoric.
(القارعة) also the Resurrection and the Hour, because it strikes (تقرع) the hearts with its terrors. القرع in the language is a kind of striking, namely the touching of one body by another with violence. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «قرعت الباب, of the pattern of نفع: I knocked at the door and rapped on it.»
(بِالطَّاغِيَةِ) by the event that exceeded the limit; what is meant by it is the Shout.
(صَرْصَرٍ) الصرصر: intensely loud; it is also said: cold. The repetition of the ṣād and the rāʾ signals its repetitiveness.
(عاتِيَةٍ) strong, violent. Further discussion of it will come.
(حُسُوماً) it will be mentioned in the i'rab and the benefits.

* I'rab:
(الْحَاقَّةُ، مَا الْحَاقَّةُ) الحاقة is a mubtadaʾ (subject), or it is the naʿt (adjective) of an [omitted] qualified noun. ما is an interrogative noun of magnification, in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and الحاقة is the khabar (predicate) of the two [Translator's note: so in the source, «خبرهما»]; the nominal clause is the khabar of الحاقة, and the link is the repetition of the mubtadaʾ in its own wording. (وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ) the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is an interrogative noun for magnification in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause أدراك is the khabar of ما. The second ما is also an interrogative noun for magnification, in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and الحاقة the khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative as the second and third objects of أدراك, because أدرى takes three objects in the accusative, and its meaning is أعلم (to inform). أدراكم [Translator's note: so in the source, for أدراك] has been suspended from governing by the interrogative. Abū Ḥayyān's wording: «ما is also an interrogative, a mubtadaʾ, and أدراك the khabar; what refers back to ما is the nominative pronoun in أدراك. ما is a mubtadaʾ and الحاقة a khabar, and the clause is in the position of an accusative by أدراك, and أدراك is suspended (muʿallaq). درى is basically made transitive with the bāʾ, and it may — rarely — be dropped. When the hamza of transfer enters it, it becomes transitive to one object by itself and to the other by a preposition. So His words ما الحاقة after أدراك are in the position of an accusative after the dropping of the preposition.» (كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعادٌ بِالْقارِعَةِ) resumptive speech, introduced to set out some of the states of al-Ḥāqqa. كذبت ثمود is a past verb and its agent; عاد is conjoined to ثمود, and بالقارعة is attached (mutaʿalliq) to كذبت. (فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, أمّا a particle of condition and detailing, and ثمود a mubtadaʾ; the fāʾ links the answer of أمّا; أهلكوا is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); بالطاغية is attached to أهلكوا, and the clause is the khabar of ثمود. (وَأَمَّا عادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عاتِيَةٍ)
conjoined to the preceding clause; صرصر and عاتية are two adjectives for ريح. (سَخَّرَها عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيالٍ وَثَمانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُوماً) the clause is a third adjective for ريح. سخرها is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the agent refers to Allah; عليهم is attached to سخرها. سبع ليال is accusative as an adverb of time, and ثمانية أيام is conjoined to سبع ليال. حسوما is a naʿt for سبع ليال وثمانية أيام; or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the accusative by a verb from its own root, i.e. تحسمهم حسوما; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of سخرها, i.e. ذات حسوم; or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). Al-Zamakhsharī's wording on this matter is excellent, and we quote it below for its value: الحسوم must be either the plural of حاسم, like شهود and قعود, or a maṣdar, like الشكور and الكفور. If it is a plural, the meaning of His words حسوما is: ill-omened days that cut off (حسمت) every good and uprooted every blessing; or continuous in the blowing of the winds, not abating for an hour until they finished them off — a likening of their continuity to the continuity of the act of one who cauterises (al-ḥāsim), repeating the cautery on the disease time after time until it is cut off. If it is a maṣdar, then either it is in the accusative by its verb implied, i.e. تحسم حسوما, in the sense of "uprooting utterly"; or it is an adjective, as in your saying ذات حسوم; or it is an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu), i.e. He subjected it to them for uprooting. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Zurāra al-Kilābī said:
ففرّق بين بينهم زمان ... تتابه فيه أعوام حسوم
(So a time separated what was between them, in which ruinous years followed one upon another.) [Translator's note: the source prints «تتابه», presumably for «تتابع».]
I say: بينهم is an adverb for the separating, except that he intended hyperbole by making the separation also be between the parts of this adverb; so he said "a time separated what was between them", and when the adverb itself is separated, its owners are necessarily separated. So it belongs to the category of metonymy (kināya). (فَتَرَى الْقَوْمَ فِيها صَرْعى كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ نَخْلٍ خاوِيَةٍ) the fāʾ is a conjunction; ترى القوم is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a mafʿūl bihi; فيها is attached to ترى, and the pronoun refers to the days and nights or to the wind, while al-Zamakhsharī referred it to its blowing-places. صرعى is a ḥāl, because the seeing here is visual. كأنهم: كأنّ and its subject, and أعجاز نخل its khabar; خاوية is a naʿt for نخل, i.e. fallen. The clause كأنهم is a ḥāl from القوم, and you may make it resumptive. (فَهَلْ تَرى لَهُمْ مِنْ باقِيَةٍ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, and هل is an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation, i.e. you do not see for them [any]; some made it for disavowal (inkār), but there is no room for disavowal here. ترى is an imperfect verb in the nominative whose agent is latent, implied as أنت; لهم is attached to ترى; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and باقية is genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is the object of ترى, i.e. any remnant, or any surviving soul, or any survival, like الطاغية in the sense of الطغيان.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «الحاقة ما الحاقة» there are two lofty devices. The first is figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī) to time, in the manner of "a night that stands [in prayer]": what is meant by it is the time in which it is due (yaḥiqq) that what was denied in this world — the resurrection — should be realised, so that in it it becomes perceptible and witnessed with the eye. It is also said it was called حاقة because it will be without doubt; and it is said it was so called because in it every person becomes deserving (ḥaqīq) of the recompense of his deeds; on these two views there is no figure of speech in the expression. Al-Azharī said: «One says حاققته فحققته أحقه, i.e. I contended with him and overcame him; so the Resurrection overcomes everyone who contends falsely in the religion of Allah, i.e. every disputant.» In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «حاقه, i.e. he disputed with him and each of them claimed the right; when he overcomes him, it is said حقه. التحاق is mutual disputing and الاحتقاق is disputing. الحاقة, الحقة and الحق are three dialectal forms.» [The second is that] in the interrogative there is a magnification of the standing of al-Ḥāqqa and an intimidation regarding its matter. There is a third device, which is putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: He did not say ما هي; the benefit of this is increased intimidation and exaltation of its standing.
2- In His word «حسوما» there is a majāz mursal (non-metaphorical figure), using the restricted — الحسم, which is the continuous application of cautery — for unrestricted continuity. It is also said to be a dependent explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya): He likened the continuity of the uprooting wind to the continuity of cautery that cuts off the disease.
3- In His words «كأنهم أعجاز نخل خاوية» there is an unrestricted simile (tashbīh mursal): He likened them to trunks because of the length of their statures; the wind would cut off their heads as it cuts off the heads of the tall palms during those eight days or seven nights. It is said they are "the days of the old woman" (ayyām al-ʿajūz): an old woman of ʿĀd hid in a tunnel, and the wind pulled her out on the eighth day and destroyed her. It is also said they are "the days of the tail-end" (ayyām al-ʿajuz), which are the end of winter, and their names are: al-Ṣinn, al-Ṣabr [Translator's note: the source prints «الضبر»], al-Wabr, al-Āmir, al-Muʾtamir, al-Muʿallil, Muṭfiʾ al-Jamr and Mukfiʾ al-Ẓaʿn.

dervis-irab:9-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَالْمُؤْتَفِكاتُ) they are the towns of the people of Lūṭ; they have been discussed before.
(بِالْخاطِئَةِ) i.e. with the sinful deed or deeds, or with sin, so that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that came on the pattern fāʿila, like العاقبة; or it is a form of attribution (nisba), like تامر and باقل. He [Ibn Mālik] said in al-Khulāṣa:
ومع فاعل وفعال فعل ... في نسب أغنى عن اليا فقل
(Along with fāʿil and faʿʿāl, faʿil in attribution dispenses with the yāʾ — so say it.)
(رابِيَةً) exceeding others in its severity. One says ربا الشيء يربو when it increases.
(واعِيَةٌ)
retaining what it hears.
(فَدُكَّتا) الدك involves the scattering of the parts, and الدق involves the mixing of the parts.
(أَرْجائِها) its sides; the plural of رجا. It is written with alif because it is of the wāw-final roots, as they say in the dual رجوان. Among the strange things about this word is that it is sweet in the plural and ugly in the singular; perhaps you will not find it in the speech of an eloquent poet, and it has not been used except in the plural, because the plural clothes it in a garment of beauty it did not have when singular. It may be used in the singular on condition of annexation. In this it differs from الأرض (the earth), which is sweet in the singular and ugly [Translator's note: the source prints «وتجمع» here, apparently for «وتسمج»] in the plural; for this reason it occurs in the Noble Qur'an only in the singular. When the heavens are mentioned in the plural, it is brought in the singular with them in every place in the Qur'an, and when it was intended to bring it as a plural, it was said: «ومن الأرض مثلهنّ», in the saying of the Exalted «الله الذي خلق سبع سموات ومن الأرض مثلهنّ». This goes back to sound taste, because it is the judge in distinguishing between words.

* I'rab:
(وَجاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَنْ قَبْلَهُ وَالْمُؤْتَفِكاتُ بِالْخاطِئَةِ) resumptive speech, or conjoined to what preceded it. جاء فرعون is a past verb and its agent; من is conjoined to فرعون, and قبله is an adverb of time attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element with no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. It was also read قِبَله, with kasra on the qāf and fatḥa on the bāʾ, i.e. "and those on his side". المؤتفكات is also conjoined, and بالخاطئة is attached to جاء. (فَعَصَوْا رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رابِيَةً) the fāʾ is a conjunction, عصوا a past verb and its agent, and رسول ربهم a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). فأخذهم is conjoined to فعصوا, أخذة is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and رابية a naʿt (adjective). The hamza of أخذة has a fatḥa because it is a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar marra), not a maṣdar of manner (maṣdar hayʾa); the sense of manner is drawn only from the naʿt. (إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَى الْماءُ حَمَلْناكُمْ فِي الْجارِيَةِ) إنّ and its subject; لمّا is a temporal adverb (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya) or a linking particle; طغى الماء is a verb and its agent; the clause حملناكم is the khabar (predicate) of إنّا — what is meant is your forefathers — and في الجارية is attached to حملناكم. (لِنَجْعَلَها لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَها أُذُنٌ واعِيَةٌ)
The lām is causal, and نجعلها is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to حملناكم. The hāʾ is the first object of نجعلها, لكم [Translator's note: the source prints «ولكن»] is a ḥāl (circumstantial), تذكرة a second object, and تعيها is accusative by conjunction to نجعل; لكم is a ḥāl, تذكرة a second object, and تعيها is accusative by conjunction to نجعل [Translator's note: this phrase is repeated in the source]; أذن is the agent and واعية a naʿt for أذن. The pronoun in لنجعلها refers to the deed, which is the saving of the believers and the drowning of the disbelievers. (فَإِذا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ واحِدَةٌ) the fāʾ is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to begin mentioning the details of the states of the Resurrection. إذا is an adverb for future time, and the clause نفخ is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. نفخة [Translator's note: the source prints «ونفحة»] is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); it is a declinable (mutaṣarrif) maṣdar, as shown by its being in the nominative, and specified (mukhtaṣṣ), because it is described by واحدة. Further explanation of this discussion will come. واحدة is a naʿt. (وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبالُ فَدُكَّتا دَكَّةً واحِدَةً) حملت is a passive past verb conjoined to نفخ, الأرض is the nāʾib fāʿil, and الجبال is conjoined to الأرض. فدكّتا is also conjoined: دكّ is a passive past verb, the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and the alif is the nāʾib fāʿil; دكّة is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and واحدة a naʿt. He did not say فدككن because He made all the mountains like a single whole and the earth like a single whole. (فَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَقَعَتِ الْواقِعَةُ) the fāʾ links the answer; يوم is an adverb annexed to another like it (إذ), and the tanwīn is a compensation for a clause composed of the two clauses نفخ and حملت; the adverb is attached to وقعت, and وقعت الواقعة is a verb and its agent. (وَانْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ واهِيَةٌ) the wāw is a conjunction, انشقت السماء a verb and its agent; the fāʾ is a conjunction, هي a mubtadaʾ (subject), and يومئذ an adverb annexed to another like it, attached to واهية, the tanwīn being a compensation for a clause, as given before; واهية is the khabar of هي. (وَالْمَلَكُ عَلى أَرْجائِها وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمانِيَةٌ) الملك is a mubtadaʾ and على أرجائها the khabar. يحمل is an imperfect verb in the nominative and عرش ربك a mafʿūl bihi; فوقهم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl from العرش, i.e. while it is above the angels; يومئذ is an adverb annexed to another like it, attached to يحمل, and ثمانية is the agent, i.e. eight angels will carry it above their heads on the Day of Resurrection; it is also said: eight ranks of angels whose number none knows but Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لا تَخْفى مِنْكُمْ خافِيَةٌ) يومئذ is an adverb annexed to another like it, attached to تعرضون; تعرضون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. لا is negating and تخفى an imperfect verb in the nominative; منكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of خافية; خافية is the agent, and the clause is a ḥāl from the wāw in تعرضون.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «إنّا لما طغى الماء حملناكم في الجارية» there is an allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya). It belongs to the category of borrowing the intelligible for the sensible because of their sharing in an intelligible matter, and it is the metaphor composed of the dense and the subtle. The thing borrowed is الطغي (transgression), which is reprehensible rising-above; that from which it is borrowed is everything that rises above others, arrogant, tyrannical and harmful; and that for which it is borrowed is the water. Transgression is intelligible, the water is sensible, and that from which it is borrowed is sensible.
2- In His words «فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة» the omission of the agent recurs in these verses. Among the striking stylistic phenomena in the inimitable discourse is the phenomenon of dispensing with the agent, which in our studies and books has been distributed among various, widely separated chapters that do not yield the secret of this dispensing. You read in morphology how the verb is made passive and the forms of the reflexive (muṭāwaʿa), and in grammar the rules of the nāʾib fāʿil; as for why the agent was omitted, that is another subject which we study in another science, the science of meanings (ʿilm al-maʿānī), which has become separated from i'rab, so that this i'rab has turned into a mere craft, whereas originally it is at the very core of meaning. Likewise we study in the science of clarity (ʿilm al-bayān) the attribution of the verb to its agent figuratively, without trying to gather up these scattered parts of the stylistic phenomenon to bring out the secret for which Arabic dispenses with the agent, attributing the verb to something other than its agent by the passive, by the reflexive, or by figurative attribution. What attracts attention is the regularity of this phenomenon in the Qur'anic discourse in one setting, which is the setting of the Resurrection, and especially in the Meccan verses, as you will see. The most the rhetoricians say is that the agent may be omitted out of fear of him or for him, or because he is known, or because he is unknown. The exegetes have proceeded to imply an omitted agent for the events of the Resurrection — Allah, Glorified is He, or one of His angels — despite the clear intention in the Qur'anic discourse to divert attention from the agent and dispense with mentioning it. The most they have said in interpreting that is that the agent is omitted because it is known. So what is the secret of the phenomenon of dispensing with it in the events of the Resurrection?

* Benefits:
For the maṣdar to stand in for the agent, it is a condition that it be declinable (mutaṣarrif) and specified, by an adjective or otherwise, as in فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة. The non-declinable maṣdar is one that keeps to the accusative as a maṣdar, like سبحان الله, and the non-specified is the vague one, like سير سير. So سبحان الله with ḍamma is impossible as the nāʾib fāʿil of its implied verb — on the basis that the original is يسبّح سبحان الله — because it is not declinable; and سير سير is impossible because it conveys no information, since the vague maṣdar is understood from the verb, so the meanings of the predicate and the subject of predication would be one, and they must differ. It is otherwise when it is specified, for the verb is unrestricted and what the maṣdar denotes is restricted, so they differ and information is conveyed. And if سير سير is impossible with the maṣdar overt, then the impossibility of سير in the passive with an implied pronoun of the maṣdar is more deserving of prohibition, because the pronoun of the emphasising maṣdar is vaguer than its overt form. This is contrary to those who permitted it, such as al-Kisāʾī and Hishām, according to what Ibn al-Sīd reported: that they both permitted جلس in the passive with an unknown pronoun in it. Thaʿlab said: he meant that it contains the pronoun of the maṣdar. Abū Ḥayyān followed them in al-Nukat al-Ḥisān, saying: "The implied maṣdar is treated like its overt form, so you may say قيم and قعد, implying the maṣdar, as if you said قيم القيام and قعد القعود." End of quote. The correct view is the prohibition. As for the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وقالت متى يبخل عليك ويعتلل ... يسؤك وإن يكشف غرامك تدرب
(And she said: whenever one is stingy with you and makes excuses, it will grieve you; and if your passion is laid bare, you will grow used to it.)
the nāʾib fāʿil of يعتلل is a pronoun of a maṣdar specified by the lām of prior reference or by an omitted adjective, the meaning being "and the known excuse-making is made", or "an excuse-making"; then He [Translator's note: so in the source] specified it by another omitted [adjective], because of the evidence indicating it, namely عليك mentioned before the verb. It was omitted just as adjectives specifying the qualified nouns are omitted when there is evidence, as in the saying of the Exalted: فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا, i.e. a beneficial one, because their deeds are weighed, as evidenced by ومن خفّت موازينه — the verse. He said this in al-Mughnī. Implying the pronoun of the maṣdar of kind was permitted by Sībawayh, because the verb does not indicate it; Ibn Kharūf said this in his commentary on the Book of Sībawayh. يسؤك, from الإساءة, is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the first condition, and تدرب, with an undotted dāl, from الدربة, which is habit, is the apodosis of the second condition. الاعتلال is excusing oneself; one says اعتلّ عليه بعلة: he excused himself to him from fulfilling his wish with an excuse. In the same way is explained وحيل بينهم with the accusative, so the meaning is "and it — i.e. the known intervening, or an intervening — was made to intervene between them", except that the adjective here is mentioned [Translator's note: so in the source]. In the same way too is explained the saying of Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd:
فيا لك من ذي حاجة حيل دونها ... وما كل ما يهوى امرؤ هو نائله
(O what a one with a need, between whom and it something has intervened! Not everything a man desires does he attain.)
So the meaning is "it — i.e. the known intervening, or an intervening — was made to intervene before it". The nāʾib fāʿil in both is not the adverb, because it is not declinable according to the majority of the Basrans. It is reported from al-Akhfash that he permitted, in لقد تقطع بينكم and ومنا دون ذلك, that the adverb be in the position of a nominative despite its fatḥa. Then Abū ʿAlī and his student Ibn Jinnī said: it is a fatḥa of inflection — and this was found problematic — and others said: a fatḥa of indeclinability (bināʾ), which is the well-known view.

dervis-irab:19-37.t:
* I'rab:
(فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ) the fāʾ is resumptive; أمّا is a particle of condition or detailing; من is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause أوتي is the ṣila (relative clause). أوتي is a passive past verb, كتابه the second object, and the first is the latent (mustatir) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); بيمينه is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أوتي. (فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ) the fāʾ links the answer of أمّا, and the clause يقول is the khabar (predicate) of من. هاؤم has two usages:
1- that it is an explicit verb;
2- that it is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl); its meaning in both cases is "take".
If it is a verbal noun — which is the one mentioned here — there are two dialectal forms of it, with and without lengthening: you say هاء درهما يا زيد and ها درهما يا زيد, and both remain so in all states, singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine. The kāf of address attaches to them as it attaches to the demonstrative, so it agrees with your addressee according to the actual case, as it does there — namely that the kāf is the pronoun of the one addressed; you say: هاك هاءك هاك هاءك, and so on. A hamza, inflected as the kāf of address is inflected, may replace the kāf of address, so you say هاء يا زيد، هاء يا هند، هاؤما، هاؤم، هاؤن, and this is the usage of the Qur'an. If it is an explicit verb — because the overt nominative pronouns attach to it — there are three dialectal forms of it. The first is that it is like عاطى يعاطي, so one says: هاء يا زيد، هائي يا هند، هائيا يا زيدان أو يا هندان، هاءوا يا زيدون، هائين يا هندات. The second is that it is like هب, so one says هأهيء هآهئوا هئن, like هب هبي هبا هبوا هبن. The third is that it is like خف, the imperative from الخوف, so one says هأهائي هاءا هاءوا هأن, like خف خافي خافا خافوا خفن [Translator's note: the paradigm forms are reproduced as printed in the source, which appears garbled in places]. Its meaning is disputed; the well-known view is that it means "take"; it is also said that its meaning is "come", so it is made transitive with إلى; and it is said that its meaning is "aim at".
The wording of al-Baḥr: «هاء in the sense of "take". Al-Kisāʾī and Ibn al-Sikkīt said: The Arabs say هاء يا رجل; for two — two men or two women — هاؤما; for men هاؤم; for a woman هاء with a hamza with kasra and without yāʾ; and for women هاين. It is also said: هاؤم is a word coined for answering one who calls, in joy and liveliness. In the ḥadīth, a Bedouin called the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, in a loud voice, and he, upon him be blessings and peace, answered him هاؤم with the force of his voice. Some claimed that it is originally compound, the original being هاء أمّوا, and then lightening and usage transformed it. And some claimed that this mīm is the pronoun of the masculine plural.»
In al-Kashshāf he confined himself to saying: «هاء is a sound uttered from which the meaning "take" is understood, like أفّ and حسّ and the like.» This is the well-known view of it. اقرءوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent. كتابيه is contested (tanāzuʿ) by هاؤم and اقرءوا: the first is made to govern according to the Kufans and the second according to the Basrans, with a pronoun implied in the other, i.e. هاؤموه اقرءوا كتابيه or هاؤم اقرءوه كتابيه. Its original form is كتابي, and the hāʾ of pausing (hāʾ al-sakt) was added to it to make the fatḥa of the yāʾ appear; the discussion of the hāʾ of pausing has been given before. The clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying). (إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ أَنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ) إنّ and its subject, and the clause ظننت its khabar; أنّ and its subject stand in place of the two objects of ظننت; ملاق is the khabar of أنّي [Translator's note: the source prints «بخبر»], and the sign of its nominative is the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns. حسابيه is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ملاق, because it is an active participle; the yāʾ is a muḍāf ilayhi and the hāʾ is for pausing. (فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ) the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that reveals an implied condition); هو is a mubtadaʾ, في عيشة the khabar, and راضية a naʿt (adjective) for عيشة. There are three views on it: 1- that it is by way of attribution (nisba), i.e. possessing contentment, like لابن and تامر for the possessor of milk and dates; i.e. contentment is established for it and permanent for it, because it is at the utmost of beauty and perfection. The Arabs do not express the greatest happiness with anything greater than العيشة الراضية, meaning that its people are content with it, and what counts in the perfection of pleasure is contentment.
2- that it is by way of showing the life as being content with its place and its being obtained by the one who deserves it, and that if the life had a mind it would be content for itself with its state; so it belongs to the category of figurative speech (majāz). 3- Abū ʿUbayda and al-Farrāʾ said that this is among the cases where fāʿil (active participle) comes in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), like ماء دافق in the sense of مدفوق, meaning that its possessor is content with it and not displeased with it; just as mafʿūl came in the sense of fāʿil, as in the saying of the Exalted: حجابا مستورا, i.e. ساترا (screening). Abū ʿUbayda's wording in his book «Majāz al-Qur'an»: "Among the figures is the passive falling to the active: the Arabs described things in their speech in the position of the active, while the meaning is that it is passive. In the Qur'an: في عيشة راضية, while it is only the one who lives in it who is content with it." (فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) for His words في عيشة, and عالية is an adjective, i.e. lofty in place and ranks. (قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ) a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is a second adjective for جنة. القطوف is the plural of قطف, with kasra on the qāf, in the sense of mafʿūl, like الذبح in the sense of المذبوح; it is what the picker picks of fruits. As for القطف with fatḥa on the qāf, it is the maṣdar (verbal noun). (كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ)
The clause is the maqūl al-qawl of an omitted saying, i.e. that is said to them. هنيئا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. enjoying it with pleasure. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «هنيئا: eating and drinking هنيئا, or هنيتم هنيئا as a maṣdar.» That is not permissible except by implying [the qualified noun], for those who permit that, i.e. أكلا هنيئا وشربا هنيئا. The detailed discussion of هنيئا has been given before. بما: the bāʾ is a causal preposition, and ما is maṣdariyya or relative; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to هنيئا, and the clause أسلفتم has no grammatical position in any case; في الأيام is attached to أسلفتم, and الخالية is a naʿt for الأيام. (وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ فَيَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ) the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause. يا is a vocative particle with the one addressed omitted, or it is merely for drawing attention (tanbīh); ليت is a particle resembling the verb, for wishing; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya) and the yāʾ is its subject; the clause لم أوت is the khabar; كتابيه is the second object, and the first is the latent nāʾib fāʿil. (وَلَمْ أَدْرِ ما حِسابِيَهْ) the wāw is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive, and أدر an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لم; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and حسابيه its khabar, the hāʾ being for pausing. The clause stands in place of the two objects of أدر, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing by the interrogative; the meaning of the interrogative is magnification and intimidation. (يا لَيْتَها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ) the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source, for يا] is for the vocative or for drawing attention, as given before; ليت and its subject — the pronoun refers to the death in this world — and the clause كانت is the khabar of ليت; the subject of كان is a latent pronoun referring to the death, and القاضية is the khabar of كانت. (ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ) ما is negating, أغنى a past verb, عنّي attached to أغنى, and ماليه the agent of أغنى; the object of أغنى is omitted for generality. You may parse ما as interrogative, in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of أغنى, so that the interrogative is for rebuke — he rebuked himself — i.e. what avail did the affluence I had in the world, which I withheld from the poor, avail me? Some parse it as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of أغنى, i.e. "what thing?", so that the maṣdar and the reference to it are neglected; the first is preferable. In ماليه it is also permissible that ما be a relative noun that is the agent of أغنى, the lām a preposition and the yāʾ in the position of a genitive, the preposition and its genitive being attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun, i.e. "that which was established and settled for me"; the first is preferable. (هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ) هلك is a past verb, عني attached to it, and سلطانيه the agent of هلك; the yāʾ is in the position of a genitive by annexation and the hāʾ is for pausing. (خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ) the clause is the maqūl al-qawl of an implied saying, and the clause of saying is resumptive, introduced to answer an implied question, as if it were said: "And what will be done with him after this lament that came from him?", and it was said: it will be said: خذوه. خذوه is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the agent and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi. فغلّوه is conjoined to خذوه, and the address is to the guards of Hell (al-zabāniya) charged with the punishment. (ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ) ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; الجحيم is a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb that what follows explains, and صلوه is an imperative verb, its agent and a mafʿūl bihi. (ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ) ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay, and في سلسلة is attached to اسلكوه; the fāʾ did not prevent that because it was fronted for emphasis and specification. ذرعها is a mubtadaʾ, سبعون its khabar and ذراعا a tamyīz (specification). The fāʾ is also a conjunction, and اسلكوه is an imperative verb, its agent and a mafʿūl bihi. Further, the two words ثم and the fāʾ occurring in the last clause: if both were for conjoining the clause فاسلكوه, it would follow that two conjunctions are combined on a single conjoined element. So ثم should be for conjoining an implied saying to what was implied before
His words خذوه, i.e. it was said to the keepers of Hell: خذوه فغلّوه ثم الجحيم صلّوه, then it was said to them: في سلسلة etc.; the fāʾ is for conjoining what is said to what is said, and ثم for conjoining the saying to the saying. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «The meaning of ثم is to indicate the disparity between the shackling and the roasting in Hell, and between that and the threading into the chain — not the delay of time.» (إِنَّهُ كانَ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ) the clause is causal, introduced to give the reason for this severe punishment he meets. إنّ and its subject, and the clause كان its khabar; the subject of كان is latent, referring to him, and the clause لا يؤمن is the khabar of كان; بالله is attached to يؤمن, and العظيم is a naʿt for الله. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «It is a giving of reason by way of resumption, which is more eloquent, as if it were said:
"Why is he punished with this severe punishment?", and it was answered with that.» (وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ) the wāw is a conjunction, to combine the two noxious matters, disbelief and miserliness, which are the vilest of beliefs and vices. لا is negating, يحضّ an imperfect verb in the nominative whose agent is latent, implied as هو, and على طعام المسكين is attached to يحضّ. (فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هاهُنا حَمِيمٌ) the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, as if it were said: "if you wish to know his end after the religious state in which he floundered, then there is not...". ليس is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and له a fronted khabar; اليوم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl, or attached to the meaning of "being settled" in the khabar. ها is for drawing attention and هنا is a demonstrative in the position of an accusative as an adverb, also attached to what اليوم is attached to; حميم is the subject of ليس. It is not valid for اليوم to be the khabar of ليس, because it is a time and what is predicated of is a body (jutha); حميم is the subject of ليس. (وَلا طَعامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ) the wāw is a conjunction, لا negating, طعام conjoined to حميم, إلا a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and من غسلين a naʿt for طعام; so the restriction entered upon the adjective, as in your saying "I have no man except from Banū Tamīm", since what is meant by الحميم is the friend. On this basis the adjective is specific to the food, i.e. he has no friend to benefit him, and no food except from such-and-such. The nūn and the yāʾ of غسلين are augments; it is what flows from wounds when they are washed. It is strange that Abū al-Baqāʾ permits making من غسلين an adjective for الحميم, as if he meant by it the thing that heats the body from the pus of the Fire — although he then went back and mentioned his statement: «It is also said [that الحميم is] of food and drink, because all of it is tasted, as evidenced by His saying ومن لم يطعمه; on this basis His words إلا من غسلين are an adjective for حميم and for طعام.» How many are the defects of transmission! (لا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخاطِؤُنَ) the clause is an adjective for غسلين; لا is negating, يأكله an imperfect verb with a fronted mafʿūl bihi, إلا a particle of restriction, and الخاطئون the agent of يأكله.

* Rhetoric:
In fronting the chain before the threading there is an important rhetorical point, which is specification; likewise in fronting Hell before the roasting. That is: thread him only into this chain, as though it were more hideous than all the other places of oppression in Hell. In specifying the length as seventy cubits there is hyperbole in intending the description of length, as He said: إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة, meaning many times; because the longer the chain, the more severe the oppression and the more painful the punishment. According to al-Jāḥiẓ, number in the Qur'an does not carry the meaning of quantitative limitation; what is meant is only multiplicity and abundance.
